name: MicroPayments – Fans Paysite: Paid Creator Subscriptions, Digital Assets, Wallet
author: videowhisper

sections.description:
Build your own fans paysite with WordPress. MicroPayments – Fans Paysite provides the foundation for a complete creator-content business: sell videos, pictures, audio, documents and posts through individual purchases, site memberships and creator subscriptions. Create a dedicated home for one creator or a platform where multiple creators manage their own work and fans discover whom to support.

Designed for site owners, entrepreneurs and developers, the solution brings the main journeys together: creators publish and offer content, fans join and buy access, and administrators configure accounts, payments and moderation. Connect the optional Video Share VOD and Picture Gallery plugins for dedicated video and picture management; the included catalog, wallets and content workspaces also work independently.

A self-hosted site gives you control of your content, customer data, branding, editorial rules and monetization choices. You operate your own platform rather than depend on a creator platform’s revenue-sharing and editorial model. There is no mandatory VideoWhisper revenue share for using this plugin; hosting, payment processing and any commission you configure for your own site remain separate.

Key features and benefits

  • Bring your library together: present posts, videos, pictures, audio and documents in Styled tiles, Cards, List, Creator feed or Justified layouts, with search, filters and ordinary page navigation.
  • Choose how to sell access: offer creator subscription tiers, individual purchases or optional one-time site memberships through WooCommerce. Describe the price, access period and purchase terms before checkout.
  • Give creators a working studio: manage their own content, drafts, prices, subscription offers and announcements from dedicated frontend workspaces.
  • Help fans find their way back: optional creator profiles, approved local avatars, free following and a private Following feed connect discovery with returning visits. Bookmarks and playback memory are separate opt-ins.
  • Start solo or grow a community: review Single creator or Multiple creators setup choices before applying them. Keep existing pages, roles, wallets and access settings.
  • Welcome each role clearly: optional dedicated fan signup, creator applications, login and password recovery work with native WordPress accounts. Leave them off when another system manages accounts.
  • Keep publishing under your control: review creator content, allow selected trusted roles or grant revocable future-publishing approval to a creator. New member content can optionally open on a calendar date or after elapsed days from its own current membership payment.
  • Make previews useful: show approved promotional images, independent public audio/video samples, duration and current offers. Add stars, likes or both with Rate Star Review.

Try the interactive content demo | Documentation and shortcodes | WordPress.org support

Popular ways to use MicroPayments

  • A single creator’s library: combine public previews, creator membership offers and individual video, picture or document purchases.
  • A multi-creator community: give creators their own profiles and studios while fans browse one mixed-media catalog or follow favorite creators.
  • A members’ resource library: sell one-time access to explicitly selected resources, with clear duration, purchase terms and private membership history.
  • An audio and download collection: present format, verified duration and file size, with separately approved click-to-play samples and optional access-checked full audio.

From first setup to returning fans

  1. Choose your creator model. Open Creator setup, review the preview and select the pages and presentation your site needs.
  2. Prepare a small library. Add native posts/downloads, or connect Video Share VOD and Picture Gallery for dedicated media management. The optional Media Capture plugin adds uploads, video/audio recording, webcam photos and screenshots.
  3. Review the offer and audience. Configure the native price or membership rules, purchase terms and publishing approval. Use the destination editor to confirm the final item.
  4. Publish and test as a fan. Check approved previews, discovery, the configured checkout and access with a separate permitted account. Fans can then return through their own purchases, membership history or Following feed.

Native catalog block and reviewed draft releases

In the WordPress editor, insert Fans paysite catalog and choose layout, content type, creator, category and visitor controls in the block sidebar. Its preview uses the existing published catalog; open the page to test filters as a separate fan. Existing [videowhisper_content_list] shortcodes continue to work. Blocks never select private buyer or creator workspaces.

Administrators can open MicroPayments > Draft release calendar from Publication readiness or the VideoWhisper toolbar. Assign site plans in the native editor first, select up to 20 eligible new drafts with no existing delay, choose a calendar or paid-start sequence and review every row. Confirm the exact preview before saving; changed content, permissions, timezone or plan terms require another review. The batch saves member-release rules, not WordPress publication dates. Publish or submit each item separately through its native editor. Existing purchases, approvals, expiry and originals stay native. The first atomic batch adapter requires core wpdb, MySQL/MariaDB with InnoDB content tables and no persistent object-cache drop-in; individual native editors remain available on other setups.

Memberships, wallets and checkout

The included wallet, catalog and content workspaces work independently. Configure creator tiers with labels, descriptions, prices and durations; an item can also have its own purchase price. Donations, goals and supported credit-package workflows are available alongside content access.

Optional WooCommerce integration adds product checkout and one-time fixed-term site memberships. Each purchase retains its own payment start and expiry; overlapping purchases do not stack unused time or renew automatically. Current paid status, ownership, refunds and expiry control access. Existing wallet, role and creator-subscription rules remain separate. WooCommerce sales do not automatically credit a creator’s token wallet.

For new member content, optional calendar or elapsed-day availability affects only the site-membership route. It does not schedule WordPress publication, approve content or extend a purchase’s expiry. Existing content is not migrated. Review and explicitly save member access before publishing; after publication, release rules can move earlier or be disabled, but cannot become more restrictive. Detailed setup and access cases are in the FAQ.

Brief purchase wording, expandable details and a selectable complete-terms page help buyers understand an offer. Native WooCommerce checkout acceptance remains authoritative. Available gateways, supported countries, fees and merchant eligibility depend on the selected extensions and provider. Qualify your site’s checkout before opening sales.

Creator profiles and content presentation

Choose eligible public-profile roles separately from publishing permissions. Opted-in profiles can show an introduction, biography, creative focus, website, approved promotional cover/avatar, collections, native content and current offers. Initials remain the default avatar. Following is free and grants neither paid access nor an email subscription.

Separate buyer views explain recorded purchases, completed WooCommerce orders and supported content currently included with creator subscriptions. Private membership history shows each source’s original term and own order link. The optional FansPaysite theme supports live light/dark/system presentation; other compatible themes remain usable.

Public previews use separately approved promotional media. Full content keeps its native audience, approval, channel, purchase and delivery checks. A hidden page does not make an ordinary public file URL private; configure protected delivery at the storage origin when needed.

Optional integrations

  • Video Share VOD and Picture Gallery: dedicated video and picture management, including explicit site-membership adapters.
  • Media Capture: a shared upload/record/review workflow. Each destination keeps its own permissions and originals.
  • WooCommerce: optional product checkout, one-time memberships, credit-package products and completed-order history.
  • TeraWallet and myCRED: optional wallet/points integrations with their own configuration and applicable extensions.
  • Rate Star Review: optional stars, likes and rating-based sorting.
  • Broadcast Live Video and Paid Videochat: optional live-content integrations with their own streaming requirements. BuddyPress/BuddyBoss and PeepSo integrations remain optional.

External services and privacy

Google reCAPTCHA is optional and is configured with the site’s reCAPTCHA keys for the guest content-upload form. When enabled and that form is rendered, the visitor’s browser loads Google’s reCAPTCHA JavaScript from https://www.google.com/recaptcha/api.js . Google receives the browser connection information, including IP address, and processes browser/device and interaction information under its policies to assess abuse. When the visitor submits the form, this plugin sends the generated response token and the site’s verification secret to Google’s verification service at https://www.google.com/recaptcha/api/siteverify . The upload’s content file, title, description and email fields are not included in that verification request. With no reCAPTCHA site key configured, the guest form does not load this Google integration.

Service information: https://developers.google.com/recaptcha/ . Privacy policy: https://policies.google.com/privacy . Terms: https://policies.google.com/terms . Site owners should explain this optional service in their own privacy/consent notices before enabling it.

Frontend account forms have their own disabled-by-default reCAPTCHA switch and keys under Accounts and creators. When enabled, the visitor explicitly checks the Google verification notice and submits before this integration loads Google. Verification sends the response token and server-held secret to the same fixed service; account passwords, email fields and profile text are not included in that verification request. The browser still sends connection and interaction information to Google. Configure keys for the site’s hostname and review current Google service terms/limits. The plugin does not create a Google account automatically.

Frontend forms use an essential, short-lived HttpOnly guest-session cookie to bind security nonces; native WordPress cookies maintain authenticated sessions. Temporary request limits use site-salted hashes and expire after fifteen minutes rather than storing raw addresses in plugin records. Creator applications retain a minimal current status/request/review timestamp. Public profile fields and private follows are scoped to the current WordPress site. Native privacy export/erasure includes these profile, application and follow records; erasure removes that presentation/community data without deleting original media, accounts, native roles, purchases, subscriptions or wallets. Deactivation retains data. WordPress controls password storage, account deletion and shared network users.

Optional payment/wallet extensions communicate with the processors the administrator configures when their checkout, funding or billing features are used. Those extensions control the payment-data requests; review their documentation and privacy/terms for the actual provider. MicroPayments stores site content, user, wallet, subscription, purchase and transaction records in WordPress; third-party extensions may retain additional records.

The included catalog and workspaces run on the WordPress site. Media storage and streaming integrations retain their own configuration requirements. Application paywalls and preview cards do not make an ordinary public media URL private; private media needs independently protected delivery at its storage/streaming origin.
sections.installation:
For optional account pages, open MicroPayments > Accounts and creators. Review the toggles, low-privilege roles and after-login destinations. Create the missing account/feed pages or assign existing published pages. Enabling frontend registration does not change WordPress’s registration setting. Keep the account toggles off when a community or membership plugin owns that workflow.

Account shortcodes: [videowhisper_login], [videowhisper_register_fan], [videowhisper_register_creator], [videowhisper_recover], [videowhisper_account]. The existing [videowhisper_register] becomes a chooser when dedicated pages are assigned and retains its legacy form otherwise. Password recovery requests a native email reset link; password selection/reset remains on WordPress’s native screen. On a network installation, registration links to native network signup rather than creating another identity system.

Community shortcodes: [videowhisper_follow_creator creator="123"] and [videowhisper_following_feed]. Follow controls also appear on opted-in creator profiles and directory cards when multi-creator following is enabled. Configure the creator home first; following is omitted in single-creator mode.

  1. Install and activate MicroPayments on WordPress 6.9 or newer with PHP 8.2 or newer. Prefer a currently supported newer PHP hosting branch where available.
  2. Open MicroPayments > Creator setup. Choose the creator mode and presentation, preview changes, then apply the reviewed setup or skip it. Configure the allowed creator, buyer and moderator roles, content types, wallet and monetization options for your site.
  3. If you will accept external payments, install/configure the required WooCommerce, TeraWallet or myCRED components and verify merchant eligibility before using real payments.
  4. Use Setup Pages to review/create the frontend pages you need, or add the documented shortcodes to existing pages. Review visibility, ownership and the destination of each page before making it available to users.
  5. Under MicroPayments > Listings, choose the public catalog layout and buyer/creator workspace layout independently. Styled tiles and Classic workspaces remain available; a shortcode can override its page’s layout.
  6. Add sample content and independent promotional featured images. The native editor’s Public preview box and the existing frontend content editor can approve a small public copy for subscription-library cards. Review the public-preview notice before saving. Check a visitor, an unentitled member, a buyer and a creator before opening the site for purchases.
  7. Configure guest submissions/reCAPTCHA and the site’s terms/privacy notices only if you intend to offer guest content upload. Public credits can be enabled or disabled in settings.
  8. On multisite, network-activate MicroPayments before using Network Admin > Settings > Legacy commerce. Activation only on a subsite does not provide this Network Admin workflow; the plugin never activates itself automatically. Ask a network administrator to review retained records there. Verify the target site, ownership/access terms and credit units before adopting records. Do not distribute one historical balance or grant to multiple sites.
  9. For a confirmed shared myCRED or TeraWallet account, use MicroPayments > Shared wallets on the relevant site as a network administrator. Review the provider account and units before approval. Unknown configurations remain unavailable; verify the intended site and provider before real transactions.
  10. Sign in as a test buyer in a modern workspace and open Included with subscriptions. Check an allowed item, an expired subscription and an item declined by its media provider. Purchase history and completed orders remain separate. Verify the hosting/provider requirements below, native navigation without JavaScript and that private workspace responses are not cached publicly.
sections.faq:
How do I prepare my first publication?

Open MicroPayments > Publication readiness, or First publication in the creator studio. Follow setup, upload/capture, draft review, separate public promotion, native publication and a separate fan-view check. Administrators see the next configuration review linked to its existing settings.

The private release-readiness timeline shows up to 12 recent editable items per page, native publication state, recent shared preparation, selected site-plan labels and calendar/paid-start conditions. It links native editors and highlights current configured term mismatches. It does not certify playback or fan entitlement, change restrictive rules, publish, approve previews, retry jobs or alter purchases/originals. Creators see their own currently editable items; administrator status still requires native object permission.

Use [videowhisper_publication_readiness] on a private creator workflow page when needed. The report uses the current account, sends no new external-service data and creates no progress or payment records.

Can I customize purchase terms and help fans find their plans?

Open MicroPayments > Purchase terms for brief plain-text wording, expandable details and a public complete-terms page. A separate purchase page is optional; otherwise the selected site terms, existing WooCommerce terms or existing public terms page is used. Actual offer price, duration and renewal facts stay visible. The disclosure appears on site-plan offers, native wallet/creator-membership confirmations, Woo product pages and classic/Blocks checkout. Native checkout acceptance and existing purchase/access records remain unchanged.

Signed-in account and buyer workspaces include separate expandable site-plan discovery and private membership history. Current access is identified before another purchase; the original source expiry remains visible. Creator subscriptions and item purchases keep their separate views. No account page, global role or billing migration is created automatically.

Full audio and private playback memory

In MicroPayments settings, open Downloads and enable the optional full-audio player. Existing verified local audio downloads can then play for signed-in users whose current native purchase, membership, collection and paid-channel checks allow access. Full audio uses an access-checked endpoint; separately approved promotional samples remain public.

Each fan chooses video memory and audio memory separately. Both default off. A prior video-memory choice does not enable audio history. Continue playing links to native item pages; Resume seeks only after the fan presses it and does not autoplay. Clear/reset and WordPress personal-data export/erasure cover private reader state while retaining purchases and other sites’ records.

The endpoint supports local files up to the existing audio metadata limit, GET/HEAD and single byte ranges. External storage/player adapters, queues and DRM are not included. Existing files are not relocated: configure private origins on your host before treating an original URL as private. An already public source URL or previously downloaded bytes cannot be revoked by this feature. Detected source changes invalidate old player URLs and positions; refresh audio metadata after replacing a file.

Private audio and video workflow

Use Add media, Review and Save in the optional shared creator workspace. Video and audio can use private originals when hosting is configured; photos and screenshots retain the native image workflow with an explicit standard-storage choice. Choose a title and content type, preview your accepted audio/video, save for native review, then set the price and audience in the destination editor. Review mode remains the default. Direct publishing still requires existing native permissions and a playback-ready source.

Private storage requires VIDEOWHISPER_PRIVATE_MEDIA_ROOT to name a readable, writable folder outside every public web root. The plugin rejects known public roots and keeps separate site/creator folders. Hosting must also ensure that no web-server alias exposes that folder. Permit WebM in native Downloads file extensions and WordPress upload settings before recording audio. WebM is included for new MicroPayments installations; existing extension restrictions are retained. For recorder WebM, configure VIDEOWHISPER_FFMPEG_BINARY and VIDEOWHISPER_FFPROBE_BINARY as trusted local executables. A stream-copy remux supplies duration/seek metadata without transcoding. Missing preparation tools retain the original privately and block handoff until it can be prepared and reviewed.

Creators and authorized staff can preview private drafts using native read/edit permissions; this does not allow staff to claim another creator’s original. Draft review is excluded from playback history. Private delivery supports qualified local progressive media using current native item access on each GET/HEAD or byte-range request. Public samples and posters require their own separate, approved files. Existing public originals are not moved, removed or made private by enabling this feature. Private HLS, CDN/remote delivery, older-source migration and universal browser/codec support are not included. Files already received cannot be recalled.

What happens to media workflow data in a privacy request?

Use WordPress Tools > Export Personal Data or Erase Personal Data. Exports include your site-local job and approval details without server paths, credentials, source tokens or other people’s content. Erasure minimizes redundant workflow titles/descriptions and actor references, revokes individual future-publishing approval and stops pending work. Minimal ownership/source references and necessary public-approval evidence remain. Physical originals, prepared media, native posts, prices, purchases and access grants are retained for separate native ownership and retention review.

Settings > Media workflow links to these tools and the privacy policy guide. Workflow details are kept by default. Administrators can review and enable minimization of finished-job details after 30, 90 or 365 days. Active jobs are excluded. A retained job cannot retry or recreate a publication; use its native item or retained original for further review.

What does private media hosting require?

The host must configure VIDEOWHISPER_PRIVATE_MEDIA_ROOT outside all public web roots and aliases. WebM preparation and video promotional generation require host-configured local FFmpeg and FFprobe executables. Durable jobs need WordPress cron or a hosting scheduler; the settings show an action notice when automatic WordPress cron is disabled. Server quotas, current creator permissions and native content access still apply. Existing public originals are not migrated by enabling private storage. Browser codec support varies; a native download remains available where appropriate.

How do media approval and background preparation work?

Open Settings > Media workflow to review approval modes. Existing plugin review settings remain effective until an administrator explicitly saves a shared mode. Recommended selected roles are administrators and editors. An administrator with user-management permission can approve a creator’s future publishing and revoke that approval from the user’s profile. Existing drafts are not automatically published. Native capabilities, seller/upload lists and content access rules still apply.

Private video/audio intake through the optional shared creator workspace is saved as a durable job. WordPress cron runs preparation; configure a hosting cron when automatic WordPress cron is disabled. Results and errors survive navigation. Check Preparation in the workspace, the native editor or Settings > Media workflow before retrying. Originals are retained. Interrupted native creation or public-copy approval may require manual review rather than repeated creation.

What does Creator setup change?

The wizard previews a separate creator home, its featured creator/content emphasis/layout and any missing shortcode pages before saving. Existing pages are reused without rewriting their content. It does not select your global homepage, install a theme, edit menus, grant seller privileges or configure payment providers. Follow the linked settings and offer-editing prerequisites before inviting buyers. You can skip or resume the preview. Undo restores only the latest setup fields; later edits block replacement. Created pages are retained, with unchanged pages returned to draft where they are not already assigned as a homepage, privacy page or menu item. When custom block navigation exists, published setup pages are conservatively retained.

How do I add an audio sample?

Open the download’s native editor or frontend content editor. Save to refresh verified duration, format and size. Upload a separate promotional audio file to Media Library, enter its attachment ID under Audio download and sample, and explicitly approve its public use. The limit is 60 seconds and 8 MiB. Samples use deliberate click-to-play controls; full paid files are not used as a fallback. Shared or cached public samples cannot be recalled by changing approval. Full-source inspection supports compatible MP3, M4A, OGG/Opus, WAV, FLAC and audio-only WebM files up to 512 MiB; browser playback depends on the encoded format. No conversion, listening queue or private podcast feed is added.

How does recorded audio become a download?

With a supported VideoWhisper recorder active, accept an audio capture and open Recorded audio drafts from your creator studio, recording page or eligible Media Library row. Review the title, description and original-file notice, then confirm creation. The bridge copies an eligible owned recording into a new unpublished download, retains the recorder original and reuses its receipt on retry. It requires existing seller, native creation and download-sharing permissions and an enabled file extension. The bridge supports a local download store under this site’s uploads and recordings up to 100 MiB. Existing recording pages are not rewritten; add [videowhisper_recorder_drafts] below the recorder shortcode if needed.

Recordings already associated with comments, activity or posts stay in their original workflow. Interrupted attempts and missing/trashed drafts retain receipts for administrator review instead of silently creating replacements. A paid draft does not make an already-public recorder original private.

Which shortcodes should I start with?

Public content discovery:

  • [videowhisper_content_list id="store" layout="grid" perpage="12" perrow="3"] – aggregate configured content types and creators.
  • [videowhisper_content_list id="creator-42" layout="feed" author_id="42" menu="0" tabs="0"] – one creator’s catalog; replace 42 with an existing creator ID.

Signed-in workspaces:

  • [videowhisper_content layout="list"] – the current buyer’s purchase history; use source=”subscriptions” for the separate Included with subscriptions view.
  • [videowhisper_content_seller layout="feed"] – the current creator’s asset studio.
  • [videowhisper_content_edit] – existing frontend item editing workflow for permitted content owners.

Wallets, subscriptions and memberships:

  • [videowhisper_my_wallet] – configured wallet and funding options.
  • [videowhisper_wallet] – compact configured wallet display.
  • [videowhisper_client_subscribe] – author subscription options.
  • [videowhisper_client_subscriptions] – the current buyer’s subscription records/settings.
  • [videowhisper_provider_subscriptions] – creator subscription setup.
  • [videowhisper_membership_buy] – site membership packages.

Content and file tools:

  • [videowhisper_content_upload] – permitted-user content upload with available media integrations.
  • [videowhisper_content_upload_guest] – optional guest submission form; configure its owner, terms and submission policy first.
  • [videowhisper_downloads], [videowhisper_download], [videowhisper_download_preview] – downloadable-file listing, item and preview tools when Downloads are enabled.
  • [videowhisper_download_upload], [videowhisper_download_import] – permitted file upload/import workflows.
  • [videowhisper_creator_stats] – creator statistics.
  • [videowhisper_donate], [videowhisper_donate_progress] – configured donations and goal/progress displays.

Use a unique id for each catalog on a page to keep shared links stable. Layout values are grid, list, feed and legacy. Public catalog filters include creator, configured content type, category, tags, title and configured access/offer categories. The refresh="30" option enables periodic refresh; static catalogs do not poll by default.

Does Feed include follows or recommendations?

No. Feed is a one-column layout honoring the selected catalog and ordering. It does not create a social network, personalized recommendations, follows or an independent chronological-post service.

How do purchases and subscription-included content differ?

Content purchases shows recorded item purchases, including expired or unavailable records without exposing a newly private title/poster. Completed orders shows the current customer’s completed WooCommerce orders. Included with subscriptions is a separate modern-workspace view of supported, published content currently allowed by both the buyer’s native MicroPayments creator subscription and the content provider. My subscriptions remains the place to review subscription records and settings. A purchase, site role or external subscription does not automatically add an item to Included with subscriptions.

What does Included with subscriptions require?

Use a modern buyer workspace layout: Cards, List or Feed. If Classic is the configured or requested layout, Included with subscriptions automatically uses Cards for that view. Saved defaults and purchase/order views are unchanged. Configure supported content types and native MicroPayments creator subscription tiers. PHP must have OpenSSL enabled with AES-256-GCM support for private navigation links. The site must permit private, uncached workspace requests; JavaScript is optional.

Each media plugin must provide a qualified complete access check. Public Video Share VOD 3.1.9 cannot qualify videos for this view. Its composed check requires version 3.1.10 or later; use its current qualified release and supported provider configuration. Picture Gallery keeps its own access rules and final veto, so an entitlement recognized by MicroPayments may still be declined by Gallery. Missing or unsupported provider checks do not grant access. Ask the site administrator to review configuration when expected items are absent; do not change a buyer’s grants merely to fill the listing.

Library cards use an explicitly approved small public preview or a placeholder, plus the item link. They do not expose the private body, original image, player, manifest or download URL. Playback, protected file delivery and external-platform subscription synchronization remain separate features.

How do I add or stop using a public library preview?

Choose a separate promotional featured image for the content item. In the native WordPress editor, use Public preview; in the existing frontend content editor, use Show a public preview in subscription libraries. An authorized save creates a separate JPEG up to 480 by 270 pixels. Reads do not generate images. Known VOD, Gallery and download source files, and Gallery-owned source attachments, are refused for this option. Local JPEG, PNG and WebP sources are supported by the preview processor when the server’s image editor supports them; the frontend uploader retains its documented upload types. This preview workflow requires local uploads served from the same origin as the WordPress site; external storage or CDN URL rewriting needs a separately qualified adapter. Ask the administrator to check uploads and image-editor support if approval fails.

That generated preview is public to anyone with its link. Turning the option off stops its use in new cards; previously shared or cached copies can remain public. Replacing a featured image requires a new approval. Public catalogs and existing purchase/creator cards retain their established featured-preview behavior and prefer an approved small preview when available. This option does not make a private-media-origin guarantee.

What happens when many candidates are declined by the provider?

The library checks a bounded candidate window and offers Continue checking if more work is needed. It does not claim the library has ended just because that window is full. Native Gallery access rules and its final veto still run for every candidate. A narrow cache optimization reuses a proven empty Gallery term inventory; custom or nonempty term queries keep their native behavior. Hosting, plugin filters and the amount of content affect response cost; no universal throughput guarantee is made.

Why does the subscription view ask me to continue checking?

The site checks content in groups and applies the current subscription and content-access rules before showing results. Continue checking looks for more matching items; it does not buy or renew anything. A view with no items may still have more items to check. Start again if an old navigation link no longer works.

Can creators keep using bulk management and announcements?

Yes. The studio links to the original Classic workflow for existing bulk/pricing/announcement operations. These actions retain their own permissions and checks. Configured upload, recording and subscription pages remain linked when available. A modern layout does not change ownership or grant another user’s management access.

Do I need FansPaysite or a community plugin?

The public catalog and included workspaces run with compatible WordPress themes. FansPaysite and community plugins are optional. Media conversion, streaming and external payment features retain their own technical requirements.

Where can I get setup help?

Start with the Installation section and shortcode FAQ. For plugin questions, use the WordPress.org support forum. Include your versions, the workflow and steps to reproduce the problem; keep credentials and private content out of public reports.

Where do I report security bugs?

Please report security bugs through the Patchstack Vulnerability Disclosure Program. Patchstack assists with verification, CVE assignment and developer notification.

How do single-creator, multi-creator and multisite sites differ?

Single-creator and multi-creator catalogs both run within one WordPress site and use the same features. Multisite adds a separate site boundary: MicroPayments scopes internal balances and commerce records to each subsite, retains ambiguous historical network records for explicit review, and requires per-site approval before using a confirmed shared external wallet. An approved shared provider account still follows that provider’s own ledger model. Cold-subsite activation alone does not establish correct financial separation; use the documented site context, legacy review and provider approvals.

What happens to historical multisite balances and purchases?

The original records are retained. They are not used as an automatic fallback for an unrelated subsite. A network administrator must review the source, target site, user/content ownership, access terms and credit unit before adopting supported records. Ambiguous records stay held. The workflow does not globally clone balances, delete the retained source or automatically change roles. Existing single-site balances and purchases are unchanged.

Are Spanish translations included?

Not in this English-first package. The Spanish PO/MO files are preserved separately as an unreviewed draft for a future localization release. Existing community language packs and custom translations are unaffected; the plugin does not force the site’s language to English.

Multisite commerce and retained legacy data

A regular single WordPress site keeps its existing wallet and purchase data model. One creator and multiple creators use the same catalog, access and commerce features.

On WordPress multisite, MicroPayments internal balances, memberships, purchases, creator plans and subscriptions are scoped to each subsite. Shared WordPress user accounts are retained. Historical network commerce records without a reliable site assignment are preserved but unavailable until a network administrator reviews and adopts them for a specific site. A balance or grant is not automatically copied to every subsite, and this review does not automatically change user roles.

A recognized native site-local myCRED account can be used in its site context. Confirmed network-shared myCRED and TeraWallet accounts require network-administrator approval for the specific site, provider account and credit/currency unit. Unknown or unavailable provider configurations remain unavailable. Approval allows the reviewed provider account to be used by that site; it does not split or isolate the external provider’s own shared ledger. Changed account/unit settings require a new review.

The native Network Admin legacy-review workflow requires network-active MicroPayments. Network administrators can preview the retained source, target site and proposed changes before adopting legacy records. Review provenance, ownership, access terms and credit units first; leave ambiguous records retained for further review.

Languages

This package is English-first. Spanish is retained separately as an incomplete review draft and is not bundled with the runtime plugin.

Where supplied, bundled translations may be generated or reviewed by AI agents. They are provided as a starting point and should be reviewed for your site before use, especially billing, access and consent wording. Translation coverage and terminology may need adjustment for your setup.

Existing WordPress community language packs and custom site translations are not removed or disabled, so some installations may continue to display translated or mixed-language text.

Optional credits and theme support

Public VideoWhisper credits are optional and disabled by default on a fresh installation. Existing explicitly saved credit-display choices are retained. A public credit link is not required to use the plugin.

Modern views include their own styles and work without FansPaysite. When that theme is active, version 2.7.10 supplies matching palette tokens and corrected additive RTL styling. Selecting a plugin layout does not change your global theme menus, page templates or archive layout.

Third-party assets and source

The bundled Fomantic UI 2.8.8 JavaScript/CSS is MIT-licensed. Human-readable source and build tools are available in the tagged upstream repository. The plugin removes its Google Fonts import and conditional Twemoji CDN image requests; typography uses available fallback fonts, and custom content can use native Unicode emoji text. Exact patch instructions, source links and hashes are included in interface/semantic/README.txt and asset-provenance.json.

Existing icon fonts are retained from the Semantic UI 2.3.3 distribution, with Font Awesome copyright notices and the SIL Open Font License 1.1 included alongside the font files. The UI code’s MIT license does not replace the font license. The bundled jQuery UI theme retains its MIT notice; the Plupload UI widget retains its GPL notice, readable JavaScript source and local text-rendering maintenance notice. Rebuild its matching minified file with the pinned Terser command in that source header.

Public text translations

With Agentic Multilingual Translator active and the relevant public text providers enabled, agents with Site Manager access can draft and separately publish translations of supported public fields. Enable drafting/publication in Translator and retain the appropriate Site Manager role, personal and connection permissions. Translating does not publish the original, change commercial access or unlock manual corrections.

Public creator profiles expose only the opted-in short introduction and biography on an unrestricted configured creator home. Authors choose a writing language from the site languages. Private account biographies, covers, offers and purchase details are excluded. The native profile publication choice and owner identity remain authoritative.

Can I sell one-time site memberships through WooCommerce?

Yes. Site membership plans are optional and start paused. Create a published virtual simple product with individual sales enabled, then use MicroPayments > Site membership plans to preview its label, product, current price and duration before enabling sales. Add [videowhisper_site_memberships] for offers and [videowhisper_my_memberships] for the signed-in fan’s source history. Existing wallet memberships and creator tiers remain separate.

Administrators explicitly select eligible plans in the Site membership access box on a post, page or native download. A selected plan can provide an alternative to existing native paid access; on otherwise free content it restricts the body. No selection changes nothing. With Video Share VOD 3.9.0+ and Picture Gallery 1.11.0+, explicitly select site plans for their configured media types too. Native visibility, password, watch/gallery and paid-channel requirements remain in force. Unknown external paid restrictions are not unlocked by a site plan. Private download/audio delivery keeps its additional native policy and qualified storage requirements. Approved public samples stay separate.

Each captured checkout grants one fixed term from the original paid date. Repurchases are independent and do not stack unused time; there is no automatic renewal. Current authoritative order/item ownership, paid status and refunds are checked locally when access is read. A line refund pauses that source; an unallocated order refund pauses membership sources on that order. Cancelled, failed and unpaid sources grant nothing. Other valid purchases/grants are retained, and no WordPress role or publishing approval is added or removed.

Native classic and Blocks checkout are supported through WooCommerce order APIs. Old/manual orders without a captured pre-payment source are not adopted. The native order action can recheck captured sources after a storage failure. Current-user history is bounded to twenty entries per page and five hundred source records; new membership checkout stops for administrator review at the ceiling without truncating history. Other ordinary WooCommerce purchases are unaffected.

WooCommerce and its gateway extensions own payment credentials, taxes, coupons and transaction/refund execution. The adapter creates no gateway account or external request and does not move wallet balances. Back up the WordPress database, including the durable private membership-signing option and WooCommerce order data; rotating native login/nonce salts does not invalidate captured paid sources. Native privacy export includes access terms; erasure retains paid-access records for review under the commerce retention policy. Pausing/deactivation retains records. Exclude personalized account, plan and protected-content pages from full-page caching.

Opt-in creator storefronts

Creators can publish a site-specific introduction from their studio or Public profile screen. Select a published item with an approved, independent public library poster for the cover; withdrawing poster approval also removes it from the storefront. Public profiles show existing membership offers and link to the native subscription confirmation flow. Browsing never processes a purchase or renewal.

Profile preferences are stored in user metadata separately for each WordPress site. Uncheck the public-profile option to hide the profile and remove its directory listing; this retains your saved draft fields and existing content. This feature adds no external service, telemetry or account registration.

The existing creator home supports a pinned single creator or an opt-in creator directory with mixed content. Single-creator sites retain the basic creator name and catalog before profile opt-in. Directory pages examine up to 12 indexed profiles and the latest 8 public candidates per profile; a creator whose recent candidates are all hidden may be omitted. The cover picker includes the latest 50 published items and the retained selection. Existing content, page assignments, wallet balances and access grants are unchanged.

Shortcodes: [videowhisper_creator_storefront creator="123"], [videowhisper_creators], [videowhisper_creator_storefront_edit]. The existing [videowhisper_creator_home] and navigation shortcodes remain supported. Optional FansPaysite mobile navigation uses a versioned read-only navigation contract; other themes work independently.

Curated collections and returning readers

Build creator-owned collections or ordered series from existing videos, pictures, downloads and posts. Open Series editor or use [videowhisper_series_editor]; storefronts show published collections automatically. Select existing items, move them up/down, choose an already approved public library poster and review publication. Contributors can submit for review; native publishers can approve the container. Each item retains its own publication, purchase, membership and provider checks. No file, product, price or entitlement is duplicated. Existing shared collection tags and URLs are unchanged.

Use [videowhisper_series id="123"] to embed an existing series or [videowhisper_series_directory] for discovery. A collection holds up to 200 distinct references owned by one creator, with twenty rows per page. Hidden, removed or reassigned items show an anonymous unavailable placeholder. Only explicitly approved independent promotional posters are used. Creator marketplaces and pinned single-creator sites share the same records and interfaces.

Signed-in readers can Save for later, including public paid items before purchase. The buyer workspace links Saved for later and Continue watching, or use [videowhisper_saved_content]. Bookmarks never unlock content. Up to 500 bookmarks and 500 playback positions are retained per user/site; pages inspect twelve records and can have gaps when access or media changes.

Playback memory is off until a user explicitly enables it. With the matching Video Share VOD adapter, supported full HTML5 videos can remember position and offer a Resume at… button. Seeking requires a click and does not autoplay. Public audio samples, hover previews, embedded/foreign players and ads/Video.js timelines are excluded. Full-audio memory is separately opt-in for supported native audio and never applies to promotional samples. Unknown duration, unavailable providers, changed media identity or expired access suppress resume. Position saves are throttled while playing and also attempted on pause/end; navigation may lose the latest unsaved interval.

Private bookmark/position/preferences records stay in WordPress user metadata scoped to the current site. No browser localStorage history, external tracking or account registration is added. Turning memory off stops recording and suggestions while retaining private positions. Explicit reset/clear actions invalidate older in-flight writes. Native WordPress personal-data export/erasure includes these records for the current site, without altering purchases, wallets or subscriptions. Plugin deactivation retains the data; account deletion follows WordPress’s native policy.

short_description: Build your own fans paysite for one or many creators, with digital content sales, memberships and creator subscriptions.
description:
Build your own fans paysite with WordPress. MicroPayments – Fans Paysite provides the foundation for a complete creator-content business: sell videos, pictures, audio, documents and posts through individual purchases, site memberships and creator subscriptions. Create a dedicated home for one creator or a platform where multiple creators manage their own work and fans discover whom to support.

Designed for site owners, entrepreneurs and developers, the solution brings the main journeys together: creators publish and offer content, fans join and buy access, and administrators configure accounts, payments and moderation. Connect the optional Video Share VOD and Picture Gallery plugins for dedicated video and picture management; the included catalog, wallets and content workspaces also work independently.

A self-hosted site gives you control of your content, customer data, branding, editorial rules and monetization choices. You operate your own platform rather than depend on a creator platform’s revenue-sharing and editorial model. There is no mandatory VideoWhisper revenue share for using this plugin; hosting, payment processing and any commission you configure for your own site remain separate.

Key features and benefits

  • Bring your library together: present posts, videos, pictures, audio and documents in Styled tiles, Cards, List, Creator feed or Justified layouts, with search, filters and ordinary page navigation.
  • Choose how to sell access: offer creator subscription tiers, individual purchases or optional one-time site memberships through WooCommerce. Describe the price, access period and purchase terms before checkout.
  • Give creators a working studio: manage their own content, drafts, prices, subscription offers and announcements from dedicated frontend workspaces.
  • Help fans find their way back: optional creator profiles, approved local avatars, free following and a private Following feed connect discovery with returning visits. Bookmarks and playback memory are separate opt-ins.
  • Start solo or grow a community: review Single creator or Multiple creators setup choices before applying them. Keep existing pages, roles, wallets and access settings.
  • Welcome each role clearly: optional dedicated fan signup, creator applications, login and password recovery work with native WordPress accounts. Leave them off when another system manages accounts.
  • Keep publishing under your control: review creator content, allow selected trusted roles or grant revocable future-publishing approval to a creator. New member content can optionally open on a calendar date or after elapsed days from its own current membership payment.
  • Make previews useful: show approved promotional images, independent public audio/video samples, duration and current offers. Add stars, likes or both with Rate Star Review.

Try the interactive content demo | Documentation and shortcodes | WordPress.org support

Popular ways to use MicroPayments

  • A single creator’s library: combine public previews, creator membership offers and individual video, picture or document purchases.
  • A multi-creator community: give creators their own profiles and studios while fans browse one mixed-media catalog or follow favorite creators.
  • A members’ resource library: sell one-time access to explicitly selected resources, with clear duration, purchase terms and private membership history.
  • An audio and download collection: present format, verified duration and file size, with separately approved click-to-play samples and optional access-checked full audio.

From first setup to returning fans

  1. Choose your creator model. Open Creator setup, review the preview and select the pages and presentation your site needs.
  2. Prepare a small library. Add native posts/downloads, or connect Video Share VOD and Picture Gallery for dedicated media management. The optional Media Capture plugin adds uploads, video/audio recording, webcam photos and screenshots.
  3. Review the offer and audience. Configure the native price or membership rules, purchase terms and publishing approval. Use the destination editor to confirm the final item.
  4. Publish and test as a fan. Check approved previews, discovery, the configured checkout and access with a separate permitted account. Fans can then return through their own purchases, membership history or Following feed.

Native catalog block and reviewed draft releases

In the WordPress editor, insert Fans paysite catalog and choose layout, content type, creator, category and visitor controls in the block sidebar. Its preview uses the existing published catalog; open the page to test filters as a separate fan. Existing [videowhisper_content_list] shortcodes continue to work. Blocks never select private buyer or creator workspaces.

Administrators can open MicroPayments > Draft release calendar from Publication readiness or the VideoWhisper toolbar. Assign site plans in the native editor first, select up to 20 eligible new drafts with no existing delay, choose a calendar or paid-start sequence and review every row. Confirm the exact preview before saving; changed content, permissions, timezone or plan terms require another review. The batch saves member-release rules, not WordPress publication dates. Publish or submit each item separately through its native editor. Existing purchases, approvals, expiry and originals stay native. The first atomic batch adapter requires core wpdb, MySQL/MariaDB with InnoDB content tables and no persistent object-cache drop-in; individual native editors remain available on other setups.

Memberships, wallets and checkout

The included wallet, catalog and content workspaces work independently. Configure creator tiers with labels, descriptions, prices and durations; an item can also have its own purchase price. Donations, goals and supported credit-package workflows are available alongside content access.

Optional WooCommerce integration adds product checkout and one-time fixed-term site memberships. Each purchase retains its own payment start and expiry; overlapping purchases do not stack unused time or renew automatically. Current paid status, ownership, refunds and expiry control access. Existing wallet, role and creator-subscription rules remain separate. WooCommerce sales do not automatically credit a creator’s token wallet.

For new member content, optional calendar or elapsed-day availability affects only the site-membership route. It does not schedule WordPress publication, approve content or extend a purchase’s expiry. Existing content is not migrated. Review and explicitly save member access before publishing; after publication, release rules can move earlier or be disabled, but cannot become more restrictive. Detailed setup and access cases are in the FAQ.

Brief purchase wording, expandable details and a selectable complete-terms page help buyers understand an offer. Native WooCommerce checkout acceptance remains authoritative. Available gateways, supported countries, fees and merchant eligibility depend on the selected extensions and provider. Qualify your site’s checkout before opening sales.

Creator profiles and content presentation

Choose eligible public-profile roles separately from publishing permissions. Opted-in profiles can show an introduction, biography, creative focus, website, approved promotional cover/avatar, collections, native content and current offers. Initials remain the default avatar. Following is free and grants neither paid access nor an email subscription.

Separate buyer views explain recorded purchases, completed WooCommerce orders and supported content currently included with creator subscriptions. Private membership history shows each source’s original term and own order link. The optional FansPaysite theme supports live light/dark/system presentation; other compatible themes remain usable.

Public previews use separately approved promotional media. Full content keeps its native audience, approval, channel, purchase and delivery checks. A hidden page does not make an ordinary public file URL private; configure protected delivery at the storage origin when needed.

Optional integrations

  • Video Share VOD and Picture Gallery: dedicated video and picture management, including explicit site-membership adapters.
  • Media Capture: a shared upload/record/review workflow. Each destination keeps its own permissions and originals.
  • WooCommerce: optional product checkout, one-time memberships, credit-package products and completed-order history.
  • TeraWallet and myCRED: optional wallet/points integrations with their own configuration and applicable extensions.
  • Rate Star Review: optional stars, likes and rating-based sorting.
  • Broadcast Live Video and Paid Videochat: optional live-content integrations with their own streaming requirements. BuddyPress/BuddyBoss and PeepSo integrations remain optional.

External services and privacy

Google reCAPTCHA is optional and is configured with the site’s reCAPTCHA keys for the guest content-upload form. When enabled and that form is rendered, the visitor’s browser loads Google’s reCAPTCHA JavaScript from https://www.google.com/recaptcha/api.js . Google receives the browser connection information, including IP address, and processes browser/device and interaction information under its policies to assess abuse. When the visitor submits the form, this plugin sends the generated response token and the site’s verification secret to Google’s verification service at https://www.google.com/recaptcha/api/siteverify . The upload’s content file, title, description and email fields are not included in that verification request. With no reCAPTCHA site key configured, the guest form does not load this Google integration.

Service information: https://developers.google.com/recaptcha/ . Privacy policy: https://policies.google.com/privacy . Terms: https://policies.google.com/terms . Site owners should explain this optional service in their own privacy/consent notices before enabling it.

Frontend account forms have their own disabled-by-default reCAPTCHA switch and keys under Accounts and creators. When enabled, the visitor explicitly checks the Google verification notice and submits before this integration loads Google. Verification sends the response token and server-held secret to the same fixed service; account passwords, email fields and profile text are not included in that verification request. The browser still sends connection and interaction information to Google. Configure keys for the site’s hostname and review current Google service terms/limits. The plugin does not create a Google account automatically.

Frontend forms use an essential, short-lived HttpOnly guest-session cookie to bind security nonces; native WordPress cookies maintain authenticated sessions. Temporary request limits use site-salted hashes and expire after fifteen minutes rather than storing raw addresses in plugin records. Creator applications retain a minimal current status/request/review timestamp. Public profile fields and private follows are scoped to the current WordPress site. Native privacy export/erasure includes these profile, application and follow records; erasure removes that presentation/community data without deleting original media, accounts, native roles, purchases, subscriptions or wallets. Deactivation retains data. WordPress controls password storage, account deletion and shared network users.

Optional payment/wallet extensions communicate with the processors the administrator configures when their checkout, funding or billing features are used. Those extensions control the payment-data requests; review their documentation and privacy/terms for the actual provider. MicroPayments stores site content, user, wallet, subscription, purchase and transaction records in WordPress; third-party extensions may retain additional records.

The included catalog and workspaces run on the WordPress site. Media storage and streaming integrations retain their own configuration requirements. Application paywalls and preview cards do not make an ordinary public media URL private; private media needs independently protected delivery at its storage/streaming origin.
